Description
-----------
<!--
Include reference to internal ticket "Fixes WB-NNNNN" and/or GitHub issue "Fixes #NNNN" (if applicable)
-->
- Fixes [WB-23822](https://wandb.atlassian.net/browse/WB-23822)

Adapts GraphQL-to-Python code generation to produce types + code that are (partially) compatible with installations of Pydantic v1.

Also restores the (generated) `ServerFeaturesQuery` pydantic classes.

**Notes:**

Because of the large number of breaking changes from Pydantic v1 to v2, these changes do not -- and cannot reasonably -- guarantee 100% identical behavior in environments with Pydantic v1 (instead of v2).

However, this PR should:
- prevent pydantic-related import errors
- make a best-effort attempt to map v2 config options / methods onto their v1 counterparts **where it's expected to impact the behavior of `wandb` API**

author: mattevans
body:
This commit introduces the ability to specify a topic ID for release notifications sent to Telegram.

The changes include:

- Added an input field `topic_id` to the workflow, allowing users to specify the Telegram topic ID when manually triggering the workflow.
- Added a step to determine the topic ID, prioritizing the input value, then the `TELEGRAM_TOPIC_ID` secret, and defaulting to '114' (Releases).
- Modified the Telegram notification step to use the determined topic ID when sending the message.
- Changed the telegram action to use curl command to be able to specify topic id.

author: tamara-builds
body:
## 🔖 Implement Bookmark Group Functionality  
Closes #57

This PR introduces full CRUD functionality for **bookmark groups**, including the ability to assign and remove bookmarks from groups.

---

### ✅ Features Implemented

- **POST** `/api/bookmark-groups` – Create a new bookmark group  
- **GET** `/api/bookmark-groups` – Fetch all bookmark groups for the user  
- **GET** `/api/bookmark-groups/:id/articles` – Fetch a single group with bookmarks and related articles  
- **PATCH** `/api/bookmark-groups/:id` – Rename a bookmark group  
- **DELETE** `/api/bookmark-groups/:id` – Delete a bookmark group  
- **POST** `/api/bookmark-groups/:groupId/bookmarks/:bookmarkId` – Assign a bookmark to a group  
- **DELETE** `/api/bookmark-groups/:groupId/bookmarks/:bookmarkId` – Remove a bookmark from a group  

---

### 🔒 Access Control

- Users can **only manage their own groups and assignments**
- Server-side validation prevents unauthorized access

---

### 🧪 Tests

- ✅ Full **integration tests** for all routes  
- ✅ **Service-level unit tests** for group logic  
- ✅ Seed file `04_bookmark_groups.js` added for realistic testing  
- ✅ Works with existing `user_bookmarks` and `articles` seeds

---

### 🧼 Extras

- 📘 JSDoc added to service and controller methods  
- 🔗 Objection.js relations added for `Bookmark` ⇄ `BookmarkGroup`  
- 🧹 Cleaned up rollback that removed `content` from articles (reverted)

---

🟢 All tests passing – ready to merge!

author: wolflex888
body:
Originally, we are expecting `loadTable` from the REST Service to return `token` as part of the config in `LoadTableResponse`. The token should have access to the table the application is interacting with.

In this PR, I am proposing to inject the token from `tableSession` that's created within `RestSessionCatalog.loadTable`. This make sense since `RestSessionCatalog` already make a request to the REST service for a token that is dedicated to interact with the table. We can use it to interact with the server instead of getting another one from the endpoint.

author: cameron-the-raven
body:
## About The Pull Request

Mostly putting this here so that it can be looked at and examined what should be done where.
This is probably butchering the code in some places, but hey, that's what it's here for.
All of these (minus the robot one and hitscan one because I checked that myself) need to be examined further to ensure it didn't break anything.

1. Removes stoplag in hitscan. This was 100% unused and seems to have been added in 6 years ago and then just...axed at some point. I don't really care to dig into it's future too much. It wasn't used, so whatever. (Doesn't need testing...Unused var.)

2. Anything involving ghost queries had their ghost query calls happen in LateInit (Tested and works https://i.imgur.com/MVWbrBr.png..Also bugfixed borers)

3. pick_module was moved from /init on robot_module to /LateInit on /robot. Triple checked to make sure it still works and yeah it does https://i.imgur.com/5rGbqIR.png (Tested and works)

4. ~~AI controlled humans had their death proc moved into LateInit  (NOT tested)~~ Gets rid of their death proc...It was unused and broken from the start. Added 6 years ago and never used. Just spawn a corpsespawn and NOT an AI mob.

5. Scrubbers only have their TGUI occur when a user is interacting with it. Splits the proc into two. One that is user controlled and one that is not.  (TESTED: https://i.imgur.com/6yOEW1o.png)

6. Corpse landmarks now do the actual death() on lateload, since that was what was causing massive problems with corpses. (Tested and works)

7. Mob chasing moved to parent instead of being on ian and the snake (Tested)

8. The TGUI input for exit_vr has been fixed by splitting the proc up. (Tested and works)

9. Promethean and protean blob sleep when they don't have humanforms upon death has been removed. (They will ALWAYS have a humanform)

10. Gets rid of the 'machine all suspend when the mapload is beginning' and swaps it to only do the atmos machinery (since those were the ones that could created, but then would have problems as it could process() before it could be init'd) (Tested and works https://i.imgur.com/VkzciPt.png)

11. More blob fixes.

This leaves ONE LAST SLEEP IN INIT and that is /obj/effect/landmark/poi_loader/Initialize

Which... InitializeAtoms and setup_atmos_machinery both have CHECK_TICK in there. Can't fix that for now.


## Changelog
:cl: Diana
del: bad code
add: good code (questionable)
fix: VR Sleepers properly exit you if EMP'd, depowered, or someone tries to pull you out of it
fix: Ghostspawns no longer multiply SECONDS by SECONDS
/:cl:

With Service being more real as a department and the addition of more granular Service job access types, it makes sense to have an access type that all members of Service can use. This PR adds Service access to Chaplain, Clown, Mime, and Musician. This PR also removes Service access from Security Cadet, Security Officer, Warden, Detective, and Head of Security. - remove: Security jobs no longer have Service access.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>BrianPugh/cyclopts (cyclopts)</summary>

### [`v3.11.0`](https://redirect.github.com/BrianPugh/cyclopts/releases/tag/v3.11.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/BrianPugh/cyclopts/compare/v3.10.1...v3.11.0)

Lots of pydantic-specific improvements in this release.

#### Features

-   Completely **disable** cyclopts conversion mechanisms for `pydantic` type hints and defer responsibility to pydantic. Notably, pydantic union discriminators now work correctly. By [@​BrianPugh](https://redirect.github.com/BrianPugh) in [https://github.com/BrianPugh/cyclopts/pull/379](https://redirect.github.com/BrianPugh/cyclopts/pull/379)
-   Add pydantic `Field.description` to the help-resolution-hierarchy. By [@​pablospe](https://redirect.github.com/pablospe) in [https://github.com/BrianPugh/cyclopts/pull/375](https://redirect.github.com/BrianPugh/cyclopts/pull/375)
-   If pydantic is used in your project (detected as pydantic being imported), pydantic will additionally validate coerced data. This means that pydantic validator types (e.g. `pydantic.PositiveInt`) now work.

#### Bug Fixes

-   Do not catch `pydantic.ValidationError` from calling user's command. by [@​BrianPugh](https://redirect.github.com/BrianPugh) in [https://github.com/BrianPugh/cyclopts/pull/378](https://redirect.github.com/BrianPugh/cyclopts/pull/378)
-   Fix empty space in HelpPanel when combining panels (introduced in v3.10.0). by [@​BrianPugh](https://redirect.github.com/BrianPugh) in [https://github.com/BrianPugh/cyclopts/pull/380](https://redirect.github.com/BrianPugh/cyclopts/pull/380)

#### New Contributors

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/BrianPugh/cyclopts/compare/v3.10.1...v3.11.0

author: chuckhend
body:
Several refactors that move operations from the postgres triggers into background worker, which reduce latency on update/inserts to source tables when vectorize job is configured as 'realtime'.

- enqueue record ids + job id instead of the complete text objects and project metadata in order to reduce overhead of serialization activity when creating embedding jobs
- moved vectorize._handle_table_update into pl/pgsql for simpler maintenance and less serialization
- move several modules from `./extension` into `./core`
- add the ability to retrieve GUC values from `./core` modules
- removed `last_completion` from the vectorize.job table (it was not in use)

body:
<!-- HOW TO USE: Under each "#### Heading" below, enter information relevant to your pull request.
Leave the headings unless they don't apply to your PR.

Please read carefully.
Once a pull request is submitted, automatic stylistic and consistency checks will be performed on the PR's changes.
The results can be either seen under the "Files changed" section of a PR or in the check's details.

Rules for suggested pull requests:
- If possible, limit yourself to small changes, 500 strings at max. Exceptions are adding or changing maps, and changes, that won't work unless they are done in a single run (even then there can be ways) - violating it puts a lot of unnecessary work on our merge team.
- Do not scope creep. If you make a pull request "Add new gun", please do not make anything more than adding the gun and following changes, like changing the stats of the gun, removing other guns from itemgroups or tweaking zombie horse stats - violating it makes future search and debugging stuff much harder, since PR name is not related to what is changed in the game. "Who the hell removed the quest item from drop in location X in PR, that adds a new plushie" - this may be a quote from a person who was affected by scope creep
- Do not make omnibus PRs. Meaning do not make a single PR, that fixes ten different, not related issues, at once, even if they are all one string - same as previously mentioned scope creep, it doesn't help to search the changes when debugging, despite all power of git blame tool

NOTE: Please grant permission for repository maintainers to edit your PR.  It is EXTREMELY common for PRs to be held up due to trivial changes being requested and the author being unavailable to make them. -->

#### Summary
Mods "[Magiclysm] Add Translocation Portal"
<!-- This section should consist of exactly one line, edit the one above.
1. Replace the word "Category" with one of these words: Features, Content, Interface, Mods, Balance, Bugfixes, Performance, Infrastructure, Build, I18N.
2. Replace the text inside the quotes with a brief description of your changes.
Or if you don't want a changelog entry, replace the whole line with just the word "None" (with no quotes).
Examples:
1. None
2. Features "In-game Armor sprite change"
3. Interface "Show crafting failure chances in the crafting interface"
4. Infrastructure "JSON-ize slot machines"
5. Bugfixes "Crafting GUI: show how much recipe makes for non-charge items"
For more on the meaning of each category, see:
https://github.com/CleverRaven/Cataclysm-DDA/blob/master/doc/CHANGELOG_GUIDELINES.md
If approved and merged, your summary will be added to the project changelog:
https://github.com/CleverRaven/Cataclysm-DDA/blob/master/data/changelog.txt -->

#### Purpose of change
Adds an advanced version of the translocator gate that allows teleporting from the gate without needing the spell

Allows easier transport from the forge of wonders / sets up better teleportation infrastructure to facilitate trading with them

Also adds a construction recipe for the new gate
- Pros: Allows fast travel without needing to know the translocate spell
- Cons: 
  - Over 2x more expensive to construct
  - Cannot use at any arbitrary location like the translocate spell.  Can only fast travel at the translocation portals

<!-- With a few sentences, describe your reasons for making this change.
If it relates to an existing issue, you can link it with a # followed by the GitHub issue number, like #1234.
When you submit a pull request that completely resolves an issue, use [Github's closing keywords](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/working-with-advanced-formatting/using-keywords-in-issues-and-pull-requests#linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue)
to automatically close the issue once your pull request is merged.
If there is no related issue, explain here what issue, feature, or other concern you are addressing.  If this is a bugfix, include steps to reproduce the original bug, so your fix can be verified. -->

#### Describe the solution
Adds the TRANSLOCATOR_GREATER terrain flag
When the translocator examine action is called, if the furniture also has the TRANSLOCATOR_GREATER allows choosing between normal attune/un-attune actions and also the translocate action, which teleports the character to any attuned translocation gates / portals

<!-- How does the feature work, or how does this fix a bug?  The easier you make your solution to understand, the faster it can get merged. -->

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
Doing something with the xedra paraclesian fast travel translocators

<!-- Explain any alternative solutions, different approaches, or possibilities you've considered using to solve the same problem. -->

#### Testing
Built a translocation portal
Used the translocation portal to translocate to other portals / gates
Attuned / Unattunded from translocation portals
Attuned / Unattuned from normal translocation gates

Inspired a bit by https://github.com/cataclysmbnteam/Cataclysm-BN/pull/6234, but decided to implement it my own way + as an optional addition rather than for every translocation gate

author: jwlarocque
body:
The image zoom effect "jumps" at the end of its animation back to its un-transformed state.  Normally the slideshow will have moved on before this happens, due to the 2s extra animation length, but if it is paused or the next image takes a particularly long time to load the jump will be visible to the user.

This PR adds a forwards animation fill to all the image zoom animations which should fix the issue.  (The pure `zoom-out` is currently unaffected since `scale(1)` is an identity transform, but I think it's probably good to put the fill in now in case of future changes to the animation.)

author: korotn3v
body:
# Knowledge Extractor component

This component add to ishell functionality to capture user actions, save them into session history, ability to create structured markdown protocols from this history and group them by tags. And ability to reuse this knowledges in the future by adding them to AI's context at the problem solving.

##  Session capturing

A singleton class, **SessionTracker**, has been created to handle logging into an SQLite database. It is responsible for recording:

- A non-blocking PTY hooks both the user’s shell actions and the AI assistant’s interactions in real time.
- Every command, response, timestamp, exit code, and assistant interactions is recorded as an atomic interaction block, stripped of ANSI escape sequences for clean downstream processing.
- The tracker starts automatically when iShell launches and remains invisible to the user.

## Persistant storage

- Captured actions and interactions are written to a SQLite database by default
- Core tables `sessions`, `commands`, `interactions`, `bookmarks` and `knowledge base` 
- All writes are wrapped in class **SessionTracker**

## Usage of knowledge base

- `markdown` comand to operate with knowladges in system mode
- supported flags to add new knowladge, add them to groups and add to assistant context
- it provide new functionality about creating, saving, tagging, showing and adding to context protocols of knowledge

author: edersondisouza
body:
Since MCUboot has a new configuration for single application slot RAM loading, add the relevant bits so a Zephyr application can be loaded in this new way. Basically, two new configurations are added to support a Zephyr application being loaded, from an arbitrary flash source, to RAM.

~While at it, remove a restriction on defining CONFIG_ROM_START_OFFSET when using mcuboot as bootloader - some platforms may need a different value there than what is currently forced.~

body:
### Description
As titled.



### Motivation and Context
We have the last MatMul in phi-4-mini onnx which is b_shape = {3072, 200064} 
packed_b_size = MlasGemmPackBSize(N, K);
 it is `3072*200064*sizeof(float)=2458386432`
This is larger than 2,147,483,647, it is out of the int boundary on a 32-bit system. Then len is negative.
So we change the type to size_t, and the model can be loaded successfully after the change.

body:
This moves the submodule to a new porting branch in the main TS repo (`tsgo-port`) which this repo will target and be updated over time.

The base of this branch includes the union/symbol ordering changes to minimize diffs. This PR includes the deletion of 338 diff files.

We'll merge from `main` into `tsgo-port` in stages over time.

When switching branches, the local checkout will be marked as dirty:

```
On branch jabaile/update-submod-1
Your branch is up to date with 'origin/jabaile/update-submod-1'.

Changes not staged for commit:
  (use "git add <file>..." to update what will be committed)
  (use "git restore <file>..." to discard changes in working directory)
        modified:   _submodules/TypeScript (new commits)

no changes added to commit (use "git add" and/or "git commit -a")
```

To switch to the right submodule, you need to run `git submodule update`.

Alternatively, one can set `git config submodule.recurse true` which will automatically do this when switching branches, at the cost of spending extra time more generally during branch switches.

author: ericywl
body:
## Motivation/summary

As we add more and more tests, I believe it's helpful to split the test runs, so that there aren't too many tests in one job (tests taking longer to run, makes checking for error logs harder etc.). 

In this PR, the active versions is moved to the workflow as a matrix instead. The test runs will then be split by version.

## How to test these changes

Run functionaltests with this branch: https://github.com/elastic/apm-server/actions/runs/14052852585.

Also tested using this PR: https://github.com/elastic/apm-server/pull/16394, and managed to cut down run time from 1h+ to 20min

## Description

This creates local scripts and github CI to generate client and server coverage reports from combined runs of unit and integration tests.

Will need to decide when to run this CI, in a subsequent PR: 
- maybe after every push to master
- or cron-like, maybe every 15 minutes if relevant code or configuration changes are detected
- or require integration tests on every push to master, and run combined coverage only 1-2 times a day since the container setup for this CI is less straightforward and likely more brittle. PR-specific coverage tests (per updated code + spec file) will be more informative and actionable.

Test:
- github: See the summary and detailed reports in a [completed Combined Test Coverage CI summary page](https://github.com/stjude/proteinpaint/actions/runs/14061959056) 
- local using container: stop local `npm run dev`, then `cd proteinpaint/container/coverage; ./generate.sh`, then click to open `index.html`'s from `client/.nyc_output` and `container/coverage/.coverage` folders. There are also markdown `.md` files in there that you can preview to compare with the github CI summary page.
- local not using a container: stop `npm run dev`, then from the proteinpaint dir run `npm run combined:coverage`

Also test that unit and integration tests from command line still work:
- `npm run test:unit` from client and server dir
- `npm run test:integration` from client dir (requires dev server to be running)

This PR implements a nix-backend, allowing mise to install any of the [>120_000 packages](https://search.nixos.org/packages) from [nixpkgs](https://github.com/nixos/nixpkgs). 

Of course, the only requirement is to be running on a system where the `nix` executable is available.

This backend uses [NixHub API](https://www.nixhub.io/) in order to search for packages versions and determine the corresponding nixpkgs revision used to install it.

Tested locally and verified everything is installed correctly.

```
mise use nix:ruby@latest
```

If you prefer, I'd add a github action that exercises this feature by installing nix and use this backend to install something.

- [x] Add tests for data store and load from localStorage.
- [x] Save relevant fields as "most recent state" in views other than explore.
- [x] Cleanup references to old ExplorePreset based sessionStorage.
- [x] Fix `grain` being added in url in pivot view.

Note that we are getting rid of the old behaviour where clearing params in the address bar would take the user to empty dashboard. This will be replaced by a home button.

The order of loading of initial dashboard state is as follows,
1. If state is present in the url, use it.
2. If no url state, load from session storage (only persists within the tab)
3. If no url state, session storage, restore last user state (from local storage).
4. If no url state, session storage, user state, apply home bookmark.
5. If no url state, session storage, user state, home bookmark, apply explore.yaml defaults
6. If no url state, session storage, user state, home bookmark or defaults open as blank dashboard.

author: oncsr
body:
## 🧷 문제 링크
https://www.acmicpc.net/problem/2912

## 🧭 풀이 시간
60분

## 👀 체감 난이도
- [x] 상
- [ ] 중
- [ ] 하
## ✏️ 문제 설명
백설공주와 난쟁이 N명이 숲 속에 살고 있다.
i번째 난쟁이는 색이 C[i]인 모자를 쓰고 있다.

사진 한 장은 두 정수 (a,b)로 나타내지며, a번째 난쟁이부터 b번째 난쟁이까지 사진에 찍혔다는 의미이다.
사진에 찍힌 난쟁이들이 쓰고 있는 모자의 색 중 절반 이상이 같은 색이라면, 그 사진은 예쁜 사진이다.

사진이 M장 주어지면, 각각 예쁜 사진인지 아닌지 알아보자. 만약 예쁜 사진이라면, 절반이 넘는 모자의 색을 구해보자.

## 🔍 풀이 방법
**[사용한 알고리즘]**
- 무작위화
---
리스트를 C+1개 만들어, 각 색상을 보유하고 있는 난쟁이의 번호를 각각의 리스트에 담아준다.
=> 찾으려는 모자 색과 사진의 구간이 정해지면, 이분 탐색으로 같은 색의 개수를 구할 수 있다.

예쁜 사진 내에 존재하는 절반이 넘는 모자를 예쁜 모자라고 하자.

예쁜 사진에서 난쟁이를 랜덤으로 한 명 골랐을 때 그 난쟁이의 모자가 **예쁜 모자가 아닐 확률**은 $q < \dfrac{1}{2}$이다.
-> 예쁜 사진에서 난쟁이를 랜덤으로 $x$명 골랐을 때 예쁜 모자가 하나도 나오지 않을 확률은 $q^x < \dfrac{1}{2^x}$이다.

$x = 100$으로만 둬도, 이 확률은 약 0.00000000000000000000000000000007%이다.
따라서, 어떤 사진에서 100번 랜덤 추출해서 예쁜 모자가 나오지 않았다면, 그 사진은 예쁜 사진이 아니라고 봐도 무관하다.

-> 총 시간복잡도는 $O(100M\log{N})$이다.

## ⏳ 회고
말도 안 되는 것 같다

author: koush
body:
This change builds on prior pull requests.

I discovered that a sack was being sent immediately per packet, rather than allowing the sack to be batched. By adding a setImmediate, allow the sack to batch many packets.

This was around a 600% improvement by reducing the strain on the event loop and network congestion.

## ⭐️ Overview > #53 아임포트 환경 구축 및 결제 기능 API를 구현했습니다. ## 🔧 Tasks - 아임포트 연동 - 결제 생성 - 결제 단건 조회 - 조건별 결제 목록 조회 - 결제 삭제 ## 📝 Additional Notes ### 1. 도메인 관련 추가 설명 - 아임포트에서 제공하는 필드명을 받아올 때, 도메인 구조를 해치지 않기위해 `@Embedded` 방식으로 처리했습니다. - 아임포트 라이브러리를 도입하는 과정에서 아임포트 도메인 클래스인 `Payment`와 이름과의 충돌이 일어났습니다. 따라서 채움 도메인 모델명을 `PaymentRecord`로 변경했습니다. - 결제 정보는 일반적으로 수정되지 않기 때문에 결제 수정 API는 구현하지 않았습니다. 추후 필요 시 환불(기부 철회) 관련 API 추가하겠습니다. - 결제 대행사(PG)는 프론트 API 연동 완료 후 더 추가할 예정입니다. ### 2. 용어 정리 - 포트원(구 아임포트): 결제 통합 플랫폼 - 채움이 각 PG사와 직접 계약하고 연동하면 복잡하므로, 포트원을 통해 한 번에 연동합니다. - 포트원은 다양한 PG사와 연결해주는 중간 다리 역할을 합니다. - PG(Payment Gateway): 결제 대행사 - 예를 들어 토스페이, 카카오페이, 페이코 등이 PG에 해당합니다. ### 3. 결제 플로우 ``` 1. 기부자가 맘에드는 펀딩 기부(결제) → FE에서 기부하기 클릭 2. 채움 서버가 포트원에 결제창 요청 → 여기서 결제창은 채움 프론트에서 띄우는 게 아닌 외부 도메인의 포트원 결제 페이지로 리다이렉션됨 3. 포트원 ~ PG(토스 등)까지 결제가 진행됨 → 포트원이 알아서 PG와 카드사 간 통신을 처리(채움 BE, FE 개입 X) 4. 결제 완료 후 결과가 채움 서버로 전송됨 → 채움 서버는 DB에 결제 성공 정보 저장 및 펀딩 관련 정보 반영 5. 기부자는 기부 완료 페이지를 확인 → 끝 ``` ## 📸 Screenshot

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [pyparsing](https://pypi.org/project/pyparsing) from **2.4.7** to **3.2.3**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 3.2.3
   ```
   ---------------------------
- Fixed bug released in 3.2.2 in which `nested_expr` could overwrite parse actions
  for defined content, and could truncate list of items within a nested list.
  Fixes Issue 600, reported by hoxbro and luisglft, with helpful diag logs and
  repro code.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.2
   ```
   ---------------------------
- Released `cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names.py` conversion utility to upgrade pyparsing-based
  programs and libraries that use legacy camelCase names to use the new PEP8-compliant
  snake_case method names. The converter can also be imported into other scripts as

        from pyparsing.tools.cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names import pep8_converter

- Fixed bug in `nested_expr` where nested contents were stripped of whitespace when
  the default whitespace characters were cleared (raised in this StackOverflow
  question https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79327649 by Ben Alan). Also addressed
  bug in resolving PEP8 compliant argument name and legacy argument name.

- Fixed bug in `rest_of_line` and the underlying `Regex` class, in which matching a
  pattern that could match an empty string (such as `".*"` or `"[A-Z]*"` would not raise
  a `ParseException` at or beyond the end of the input string. This could cause an
  infinite parsing loop when parsing `rest_of_line` at the end of the input string.
  Reported by user Kylotan, thanks! (Issue 593)

- Enhancements and extra input validation for `pyparsing.util.make_compressed_re` - see
  usage in `examples/complex_chemical_formulas.py` and result in the generated railroad
  diagram `examples/complex_chemical_formulas_diagram.html`. Properly escapes characters
  like "." and "*" that have special meaning in regular expressions.

- Fixed bug in `one_of()` to properly escape characters that are regular expression markers
  (such as '*', '+', '?', etc.) before building the internal regex.

- Better exception message for `MatchFirst` and `Or` expressions, showing all alternatives
  rather than just the first one. Fixes Issue 592, reported by Focke, thanks!

- Added return type annotation of "-> None" for all `__init__()` methods, to satisfy
  `mypy --strict` type checking. PR submitted by FeRD, thank you!

- Added optional argument `show_hidden` to `create_diagram` to show
  elements that are used internally by pyparsing, but are not part of the actual
  parser grammar. For instance, the `Tag` class can insert values into the parsed
  results but it does not actually parse any input, so by default it is not included
  in a railroad diagram. By calling `create_diagram` with `show_hidden` = `True`,
  these internal elements will be included. (You can see this in the tag_metadata.py
  script in the examples directory.)

- Fixed bug in `number_words.py` example. Also added `ebnf_number_words.py` to demonstrate
  using the `ebnf.py` EBNF parser generator to build a similar parser directly from
  EBNF.

- Fixed syntax warning raised in `bigquery_view_parser.py`, invalid escape sequence "\s".
  Reported by sameer-google, nice catch! (Issue 598)

- Added support for Python 3.14.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.1
   ```
   ------------------------------
- Updated generated railroad diagrams to make non-terminal elements links to their related
  sub-diagrams. This _greatly_ improves navigation of the diagram, especially for
  large, complex parsers.

- Simplified railroad diagrams emitted for parsers using `infix_notation`, by hiding
  lookahead terms. Renamed internally generated expressions for clarity, and improved
  diagramming.

- Improved performance of `cpp_style_comment`, `c_style_comment`, `common.fnumber`
  and `common.ieee_float` Regex expressions. PRs submitted by Gabriel Gerlero,
  nice work, thanks!

- Add missing type annotations to `match_only_at_col`, `replace_with`, `remove_quotes`,
  `with_attribute`, and `with_class`. Issue 585 reported by rafrafrek.

- Added generated diagrams for many of the examples.

- Replaced old `examples/0README.html` file with `examples/README.md` file.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.0
   ```
   -------------------------------
- Discontinued support for Python 3.6, 3.7, and 3.8. Adopted new Python features from
  Python versions 3.7-3.9:
  - Updated type annotations to use built-in container types instead of names
    imported from the `typing` module (e.g., `list[str]` vs `List[str]`).
  - Reworked portions of the packrat cache to leverage insertion-preserving ordering
    in dicts (including removal of uses of `OrderedDict`).
  - Changed `pdb.set_trace()` call in `ParserElement.set_break()` to `breakpoint()`.
  - Converted `typing.NamedTuple` to `dataclasses.dataclass` in railroad diagramming
    code.
  - Added `from __future__ import annotations` to clean up some type annotations.
  (with assistance from ISyncWithFoo, issue 535, thanks for the help!)

- POSSIBLE BREAKING CHANGES

    The following bugfixes may result in subtle changes in the results returned or
    exceptions raised by pyparsing.

    - Fixed code in `ParseElementEnhance` subclasses that
      replaced detailed exception messages raised in contained expressions with a
      less-specific and less-informative generic exception message and location.

      If your code has conditional logic based on the message content in raised
      `ParseExceptions`, this bugfix may require changes in your code.

    - Fixed bug in `transform_string()` where whitespace
      in the input string was not properly preserved in the output string.

      If your code uses `transform_string`, this bugfix may require changes in
      your code.

    - Fixed bug where an `IndexError` raised in a parse action was
      incorrectly handled as an `IndexError` raised as part of the `ParserElement`
      parsing methods, and reraised as a `ParseException`. Now an `IndexError`
      that raises inside a parse action will properly propagate out as an `IndexError`.
      (Issue 573, reported by August Karlstedt, thanks!)

      If your code raises `IndexError`s in parse actions, this bugfix may require
      changes in your code.

- FIXES AND NEW FEATURES

    - Added type annotations to remainder of `pyparsing` package, and added `mypy`
      run to `tox.ini`, so that type annotations are now run as part of pyparsing's CI.
      Addresses Issue 373, raised by Iwan Aucamp, thanks!

    - Exception message format can now be customized, by overriding
      `ParseBaseException.format_message`:

          def custom_exception_message(exc) -> str:
              found_phrase = f", found {exc.found}" if exc.found else ""
              return f"{exc.lineno}:{exc.column} {exc.msg}{found_phrase}"

          ParseBaseException.formatted_message = custom_exception_message

      (PR 571 submitted by Odysseyas Krystalakos, nice work!)

    - `run_tests` now detects if an exception is raised in a parse action, and will
      report it with an enhanced error message, with the exception type, string,
      and parse action name.

    - `QuotedString` now handles translation of escaped integer, hex, octal, and
      Unicode sequences to their corresponding characters.

    - Fixed the displayed output of `Regex` terms to deduplicate repeated backslashes,
      for easier reading in debugging, printing, and railroad diagrams.

    - Fixed (or at least reduced) elusive bug when generating railroad diagrams,
      where some diagram elements were just empty blocks. Fix submitted by RoDuth,

author: wujianchi
body:
## 红黑树实现及遍历算法

本PR由cardove实现，提供了一个完整的红黑树实现，以及四种常见的树遍历算法：

### 主要内容

1. 实现了红黑树的基本结构和插入操作
2. 实现了四种遍历方式：
   - 前序遍历 (Pre-order Traversal)
   - 中序遍历 (In-order Traversal)
   - 后序遍历 (Post-order Traversal)
   - 层序遍历 (Level-order Traversal)
3. 提供了简单的演示类，展示各种遍历的效果
4. 更新了README文档

### 技术细节

- 红黑树的自平衡通过左旋、右旋和颜色翻转实现
- 所有遍历算法均采用递归方式实现
- 层序遍历通过计算树高度并逐层打印实现

### 测试方法

运行`RedBlackTreeDemo`类可以查看演示效果。

author: haetae-bit
body:
A number of changes were made - mainly switching from tabs component to a table component.

Tabs were discarded for the following reasons:
- Searching through tabs would've been a PITA to implement
- This limited the amount of data viewable to visitors, which would probably not be great for UX since people want to see _all_ data before filtering through it
- Initial design wasn't super great for accessibility, although it seemed convenient at first

Used Alpine.js to create the table, with filtering and searching, but sorting is still kind of WIP. Might look into other premade table components that might have better implementations?

Search is limited to `/archive`, implemented with Fuse.js. I had too much trouble with Pagefind not indexing the data properly. The implementation used for `/archive` can pretty much be reused for the wiki section.

To do:
- [ ] Set up structure the section for textual guides
- [ ] Set up styles for the table
- [ ] Clean up fallback pages and add some more links there
- [ ] Nail down an actual CMS integration (_maybe_ Decap CMS instead of PagesCMS for live preview?)

body:
ビデオチャットサンプル、サイマルキャストサンプル、スポットライトサンプルの映像コーデックのリストに `未指定` を追加しました。
スクリーンキャストサンプルには追加していません。サンプルの用途ととして未指定を設定することが重要ではないと考えたためです。

また、合わせて映像コーデックのまた、合わせて映像コーデックのリスト順序を統一しました。
Sora のドキュメントに合わせた順序としています。

---

This pull request includes updates to the Sora Android SDK and several sample applications to improve video codec handling and unify the display order of codec options. The most important changes include upgrading the SDK, adding an "unspecified" option for video codecs, and standardizing the codec list order.

### SDK and Codec Updates:

* Upgraded Sora Android SDK to version 2025.2.0. (`CHANGES.md`)
* Added "unspecified" (`未指定`) option for video codecs in the video chat, simulcast, and spotlight samples. (`SoraScreencastServiceStarter.kt`, `SimulcastSetupActivity.kt`, `SpotlightRoomSetupActivity.kt`, `VideoChatRoomSetupActivity.kt`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-90e1d2c607bed708558c3f4461627d08db4a76b25901a4537aa7966860f2ab18L25-R25) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e77e9e271e73ad7ca2019d27254a824b79cdefee66d61dbe31704d6d7ba8a537L18-R18) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5497832fb280c0f77e6bdfe24d59be3251b90ddf5a8cb8270765e08dfdff3029L19-R19) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-0c77db01fc96080fd46bda83bcaf54fb72a51f6c129ad21ba8ec4b96b61754a9L18-R18)

### Codec Default Adjustments:

* Changed default video codec to `SoraVideoOption.Codec.DEFAULT` in multiple classes. (`SoraVideoChannel.kt`, `SimulcastActivity.kt`, `VideoChatRoomActivity.kt`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-899cf7959590c171f4375279027642cc8bf4ee509cc350f645dcce5873ed062cL64-R64) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4efbc77a1baea834716efa6d5f1556e80abe6627b4e818b284e358e2d9345c8dL45-R45) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-dac9d2ad04cf2d76bf2ca85dd8a93c04a6b5658af7ccf9370da3e15a0a342d25L45-R45)

### Codec List Order Standardization:

* Unified the display order of video codec options across different activities. (`ScreencastSetupActivity.kt`, `SimulcastSetupActivity.kt`, `SpotlightRoomSetupActivity.kt`, `VideoChatRoomSetupActivity.kt`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-79c316d066ff23b321399cc98070d3fb080f5537c6231f9b2885d4b6c58292a8L23-R23) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e77e9e271e73ad7ca2019d27254a824b79cdefee66d61dbe31704d6d7ba8a537L18-R18) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-5497832fb280c0f77e6bdfe24d59be3251b90ddf5a8cb8270765e08dfdff3029L19-R19) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-0c77db01fc96080fd46bda83bcaf54fb72a51f6c129ad21ba8ec4b96b61754a9L18-R18)

body: ## Description This PR implements a mini calendar popup for the DatePicker component, enhancing the date selection UX by allowing users to visually select dates rather than typing them manually. ## Key changes: - Added MiniCalendar integration to the DatePicker component - Implemented proper focus/blur handling for seamless calendar interaction - Ensured consistent date formatting between typed input and calendar selection - Fixed validation issues to prevent erroneous error messages - Added proper event handling to maintain the component's existing behavior ## Testing 1. Navigate to any form page that uses the DatePicker component 2. Click on a date field to focus it - Verify that the mini calendar appears below the input 3. Select a date from the calendar - The calendar should close - The input should show the date in the formatted style (e.g., "January 1, 2023") - No error messages should appear 4. Test typing a date manually - Enter a valid date in MM/DD/YYYY format - Click away and verify it formats correctly - Enter an invalid date and verify the error message appears 5. Test moving between different date fields - Verify that selecting from one calendar then another maintains proper formatting - Verify that clicking outside the component closes the calendar ## Implementation Notes - The implementation maintains backward compatibility with the existing DatePicker behavior - Added minimal styling to ensure the calendar displays correctly - Added date conversion utilities to properly communicate between string dates and the calendar component - Ensured clean state management to prevent validation errors when selecting from the calendar ## Changes Made - Modified DatePicker component to conditionally render MiniCalendar - Added click-outside handler to close the calendar when clicking elsewhere - Enhanced date validation to handle both formatted and unformatted dates - Implemented date conversion utilities for calendar integration - Added proper styles for the calendar popup container ## Issues - DatePicker was changed in both the FormValidation PR and this one, please merge accordingly! ## Images Closes #116

<details>
<summary>actions/setup-python (actions/setup-python)</summary>

### [`v5.5.0`](https://redirect.github.com/actions/setup-python/releases/tag/v5.5.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/actions/setup-python/compare/v5.4.0...v5.5.0)

#### What's Changed

##### Enhancements:

-   Support free threaded Python versions like '3.13t' by [@​colesbury](https://redirect.github.com/colesbury) in [https://github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/973](https://redirect.github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/973)
-   Enhance Workflows: Include ubuntu-arm runners, Add e2e Testing for free threaded and Upgrade [@​action/cache](https://redirect.github.com/action/cache) from 4.0.0 to 4.0.3 by [@​priya-kinthali](https://redirect.github.com/priya-kinthali) in [https://github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/1056](https://redirect.github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/1056)
-   Add support for .tool-versions file in setup-python by [@​mahabaleshwars](https://redirect.github.com/mahabaleshwars) in [https://github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/1043](https://redirect.github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/1043)

##### Bug fixes:

-   Fix architecture for pypy on Linux ARM64 by [@​mayeut](https://redirect.github.com/mayeut) in [https://github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/1011](https://redirect.github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/1011)
    This update maps arm64 to aarch64 for Linux ARM64 PyPy installations.

##### Dependency updates:

-   Upgrade [@​vercel/ncc](https://redirect.github.com/vercel/ncc) from 0.38.1 to 0.38.3 by [@​dependabot](https://redirect.github.com/dependabot) in [https://github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/1016](https://redirect.github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/1016)
-   Upgrade [@​actions/glob](https://redirect.github.com/actions/glob) from 0.4.0 to 0.5.0 by [@​dependabot](https://redirect.github.com/dependabot) in [https://github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/1015](https://redirect.github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/1015)

#### New Contributors

-   [@​colesbury](https://redirect.github.com/colesbury) made their first contribution in [https://github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/973](https://redirect.github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/973)
-   [@​mahabaleshwars](https://redirect.github.com/mahabaleshwars) made their first contribution in [https://github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/1043](https://redirect.github.com/actions/setup-python/pull/1043)

author: ktaka-ccmp
body:
This commit reorganizes the library's structure to improve maintainability and user experience:

- Rename /summary routes to /user for better semantic clarity
- Add centralized configuration with O2P_REDIRECT_ANON and O2P_REDIRECT_USER
- Move page handlers to a dedicated pages module with proper organization
- Simplify demo integration by using library-provided redirects
- Fix formatting and add trace logging in security checks
- Hide user ID from summary page UI for better security
- Consolidate templates and remove redundant code

This refactoring makes the library more modular, easier to maintain, and provides better defaults for integrators while maintaining all existing functionality.

[Cocoa] Remove unnecessary CoreText soft linking
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=290373

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [pyparsing](https://pypi.org/project/pyparsing) from **2.4.7** to **3.2.3**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 3.2.3
   ```
   ---------------------------
- Fixed bug released in 3.2.2 in which `nested_expr` could overwrite parse actions
  for defined content, and could truncate list of items within a nested list.
  Fixes Issue 600, reported by hoxbro and luisglft, with helpful diag logs and
  repro code.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.2
   ```
   ---------------------------
- Released `cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names.py` conversion utility to upgrade pyparsing-based
  programs and libraries that use legacy camelCase names to use the new PEP8-compliant
  snake_case method names. The converter can also be imported into other scripts as

        from pyparsing.tools.cvt_pyparsing_pep8_names import pep8_converter

- Fixed bug in `nested_expr` where nested contents were stripped of whitespace when
  the default whitespace characters were cleared (raised in this StackOverflow
  question https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79327649 by Ben Alan). Also addressed
  bug in resolving PEP8 compliant argument name and legacy argument name.

- Fixed bug in `rest_of_line` and the underlying `Regex` class, in which matching a
  pattern that could match an empty string (such as `".*"` or `"[A-Z]*"` would not raise
  a `ParseException` at or beyond the end of the input string. This could cause an
  infinite parsing loop when parsing `rest_of_line` at the end of the input string.
  Reported by user Kylotan, thanks! (Issue 593)

- Enhancements and extra input validation for `pyparsing.util.make_compressed_re` - see
  usage in `examples/complex_chemical_formulas.py` and result in the generated railroad
  diagram `examples/complex_chemical_formulas_diagram.html`. Properly escapes characters
  like "." and "*" that have special meaning in regular expressions.

- Fixed bug in `one_of()` to properly escape characters that are regular expression markers
  (such as '*', '+', '?', etc.) before building the internal regex.

- Better exception message for `MatchFirst` and `Or` expressions, showing all alternatives
  rather than just the first one. Fixes Issue 592, reported by Focke, thanks!

- Added return type annotation of "-> None" for all `__init__()` methods, to satisfy
  `mypy --strict` type checking. PR submitted by FeRD, thank you!

- Added optional argument `show_hidden` to `create_diagram` to show
  elements that are used internally by pyparsing, but are not part of the actual
  parser grammar. For instance, the `Tag` class can insert values into the parsed
  results but it does not actually parse any input, so by default it is not included
  in a railroad diagram. By calling `create_diagram` with `show_hidden` = `True`,
  these internal elements will be included. (You can see this in the tag_metadata.py
  script in the examples directory.)

- Fixed bug in `number_words.py` example. Also added `ebnf_number_words.py` to demonstrate
  using the `ebnf.py` EBNF parser generator to build a similar parser directly from
  EBNF.

- Fixed syntax warning raised in `bigquery_view_parser.py`, invalid escape sequence "\s".
  Reported by sameer-google, nice catch! (Issue 598)

- Added support for Python 3.14.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.1
   ```
   ------------------------------
- Updated generated railroad diagrams to make non-terminal elements links to their related
  sub-diagrams. This _greatly_ improves navigation of the diagram, especially for
  large, complex parsers.

- Simplified railroad diagrams emitted for parsers using `infix_notation`, by hiding
  lookahead terms. Renamed internally generated expressions for clarity, and improved
  diagramming.

- Improved performance of `cpp_style_comment`, `c_style_comment`, `common.fnumber`
  and `common.ieee_float` Regex expressions. PRs submitted by Gabriel Gerlero,
  nice work, thanks!

- Add missing type annotations to `match_only_at_col`, `replace_with`, `remove_quotes`,
  `with_attribute`, and `with_class`. Issue 585 reported by rafrafrek.

- Added generated diagrams for many of the examples.

- Replaced old `examples/0README.html` file with `examples/README.md` file.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.2.0
   ```
   -------------------------------
- Discontinued support for Python 3.6, 3.7, and 3.8. Adopted new Python features from
  Python versions 3.7-3.9:
  - Updated type annotations to use built-in container types instead of names
    imported from the `typing` module (e.g., `list[str]` vs `List[str]`).
  - Reworked portions of the packrat cache to leverage insertion-preserving ordering
    in dicts (including removal of uses of `OrderedDict`).
  - Changed `pdb.set_trace()` call in `ParserElement.set_break()` to `breakpoint()`.
  - Converted `typing.NamedTuple` to `dataclasses.dataclass` in railroad diagramming
    code.
  - Added `from __future__ import annotations` to clean up some type annotations.
  (with assistance from ISyncWithFoo, issue 535, thanks for the help!)

- POSSIBLE BREAKING CHANGES

    The following bugfixes may result in subtle changes in the results returned or
    exceptions raised by pyparsing.

    - Fixed code in `ParseElementEnhance` subclasses that
      replaced detailed exception messages raised in contained expressions with a
      less-specific and less-informative generic exception message and location.

      If your code has conditional logic based on the message content in raised
      `ParseExceptions`, this bugfix may require changes in your code.

    - Fixed bug in `transform_string()` where whitespace
      in the input string was not properly preserved in the output string.

      If your code uses `transform_string`, this bugfix may require changes in
      your code.

    - Fixed bug where an `IndexError` raised in a parse action was
      incorrectly handled as an `IndexError` raised as part of the `ParserElement`
      parsing methods, and reraised as a `ParseException`. Now an `IndexError`
      that raises inside a parse action will properly propagate out as an `IndexError`.
      (Issue 573, reported by August Karlstedt, thanks!)

      If your code raises `IndexError`s in parse actions, this bugfix may require
      changes in your code.

- FIXES AND NEW FEATURES

    - Added type annotations to remainder of `pyparsing` package, and added `mypy`
      run to `tox.ini`, so that type annotations are now run as part of pyparsing's CI.
      Addresses Issue 373, raised by Iwan Aucamp, thanks!

    - Exception message format can now be customized, by overriding
      `ParseBaseException.format_message`:

          def custom_exception_message(exc) -> str:
              found_phrase = f", found {exc.found}" if exc.found else ""
              return f"{exc.lineno}:{exc.column} {exc.msg}{found_phrase}"

          ParseBaseException.formatted_message = custom_exception_message

      (PR 571 submitted by Odysseyas Krystalakos, nice work!)

    - `run_tests` now detects if an exception is raised in a parse action, and will
      report it with an enhanced error message, with the exception type, string,
      and parse action name.

    - `QuotedString` now handles translation of escaped integer, hex, octal, and
      Unicode sequences to their corresponding characters.

    - Fixed the displayed output of `Regex` terms to deduplicate repeated backslashes,
      for easier reading in debugging, printing, and railroad diagrams.

    - Fixed (or at least reduced) elusive bug when generating railroad diagrams,
      where some diagram elements were just empty blocks. Fix submitted by RoDuth,
      thanks a ton!

    - Fixed railroad diagrams that get generated with a parser containing a Regex element
      defined using a verbose pattern - the pattern gets flattened and comments removed
      before creating the corresponding diagram eleme

body:
<!--
Thanks for contributing to Rails!

Please do not make *Draft* pull requests, as they still send
notifications to everyone watching the Rails repo.

Create a pull request when it is ready for review and feedback
from the Rails team :).

If your pull request affects documentation or any non-code
changes, guidelines for those changes are [available
here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#contributing-to-the-rails-documentation)

About this template

The following template aims to help contributors write a good description for their pull requests.
We'd like you to provide a description of the changes in your pull request (i.e. bugs fixed or features added), the motivation behind the changes, and complete the checklist below before opening a pull request.

Feel free to discard it if you need to (e.g. when you just fix a typo). -->

### Motivation / Background

ActiveStorage currently does not handle multi db support, as mentioned in this [discussion](https://discuss.rubyonrails.org/t/activestorage-multi-db-support/80123/2).

This Pull Request has been created because I work a on project using three databases on the same application. Two of those databases use ActiveStorage and I need therefore this feature.

### Detail

- I moved most of the app folders and files in the lib folder since most of the classes are now created dynamically through meta-programming ;
- I left the whole thing as an engine to properly and easily handle migrations and javascript related files ;
- I added a new initializer which is run after the app has been initialized to create the blob, attachment and variant_record needed models, controllers and jobs based on app config (which provides the db name and connection class for each case) ;
- since the dummy test application is run in two different configurations for single or multi db, I created two separated rake tasks to be run separately for testing ;
- the services are only tested in the single_db tests since they do not directly involve named blob, attachment or variant_record classes ;
- I tested my solution on local apps using single db and multi db, both worked.

### Additional information

I made the choice to make the old blob/attachment/variant classes as modules included in the dynamically generated classes. I could also have used inheritance but I find it more readable and flexible this way.

One test keeps failing:
- `eager_loading_has_many_attached_records` for `variant_record_test`, 12 requests are performed instead of 10, I cannot manage to fix it.

The rotating image related test in vips_test.rb was already failing on main branch.

I did not change the CHANGELOG yet since I wanted to have a feedback on the philosophy I followed here first.
If we agree on the solution I used here, I will also adapt test failing in other rails gems since they break on CI.

### Checklist

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [x] This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
* [x] Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: `[Fix #issue-number]`
* [x] Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature.
* [ ] CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature. Minor bug fixes and documentation changes should not be included.

body:
# Implement String Search Function in File

## Task
Write a function to search for a specific string in a file.

## Acceptance Criteria
All tests must pass.

## Summary of Changes
Added a new utility function to search for a specific string within a file. The function takes a file path and a search string as input, and returns the line numbers and content of lines containing the search string.

## Test Cases
 - Verify the function returns correct line numbers when a string is found
 - Confirm function handles cases where the string is not present in the file
 - Test function with empty file input
 - Ensure function works with case-sensitive and case-insensitive search options
 - Validate function performance with large files

author: henfo
body:
For issue #411.

This change to the MapModel.addLayer API, allows the developer to insert a new layer at a specified position. The position can be defined as absolute or relative position to a different layer.
For a project, I implemented this feature the following way:
The developer can provide an option if they want the new layer to be at the "top" (default), "bottom", "above" or "below" a layer with a specific ID, or at an "index" in the top-level hierarchy.

This adds a small overhead, since the zIndex needs to be updated for every layer when a change occurs. However, I don't think any project would ever get near a layer count where a linear scan on an insert or remove would harm performance.

----

Edit: final API implemented in this PR, copied over from changeset:


Top level operational layers can now be inserted at an arbitrary position.

```ts
const mapModel = ...;
const newLayer = new SimpleLayer({
    title: "New layer",
    // ...
});

mapModel.layers.addLayer(newLayer, { at: "top" }); // Same as default: on top of all existing operational layers
mapModel.layers.addLayer(newLayer, { at: "bottom" }); // Below all other operational layers

const otherLayer = ...; // Eiter a valid layer id or a layer instance. Must be from the same collection.
mapModel.layers.addLayer(newLayer, { at: "above", reference: otherLayer }); // Above the reference layer
mapModel.layers.addLayer(newLayer, { at: "below", reference: otherLayer }); // Below the reference layer
```

# Question Creator Implementation

## Overview
Added a new Question Creator feature that allows users to create different types of questions for the learning platform.

## Features
- Multiple Choice questions
- Sentence Builder questions
- Fill in the Blanks questions

Each question type includes:
- Question-specific content fields
- Metadata (English level, difficulty, category)
- Game settings (points, time limit, difficulty multiplier)

## Technical Details
- Implemented using React components with hooks
- Uses shared UI components from layout library
- Integrates with questionsApi service
- Includes form validation and error handling
- Follows API schema structure for question data

## Evidence after Solution
 **Video**: [Link to Loom video](https://www.loom.com/share/a7944555506f4cefa9a6964f8569a7a0?sid=4075cb70-7bc1-48c8-b2f9-58878c14f8d8)

## Testing
- [ ] Test form validation for all question types
- [ ] Verify API integration
- [ ] Check error handling and notifications
- [ ] Test form reset after submission

** Closes #115 **

author: sinclert-canonical
body:
This PR fixes the PostgreSQL client in order to avoid issuing `GRANT` and `REVOKE` queries when either the list of groups or the list of users is empty.

This is a **quality of life improvement** for package users that do not want to defensively check for empty lists before calling the `grant_group_memberships` and `revoke_group_memberships` methods. The SQL syntax exceptions were never raised to the package user code as they were intercepted [here](https://github.com/canonical/postgresql-ldap-sync/blob/adfec22277bdbd7b5cbf97903ce3d485f94a5786/src/postgresql_ldap_sync/clients/psql/postgres.py#L132-L133) and [here](https://github.com/canonical/postgresql-ldap-sync/blob/adfec22277bdbd7b5cbf97903ce3d485f94a5786/src/postgresql_ldap_sync/clients/psql/postgres.py#L147-L148), but it would be nice to avoid seeing errors in the logs.

author: ucwong
body:
Currently, even though it takes in a `Logger` interface, `log.SetDefualt` enforces that the concrete type of the provided logger is `*logger` because:
1. in `init` `root.Store` is called with a `*logger`
2. `atomic.Value` panics if the concrete type provided in `Store` is not consistent across calls.
([ref](https://pkg.go.dev/sync/atomic#Value.Store))

> All calls to Store for a given Value must use values of the same
concrete type.

This PR changes to use `sync.RWMutex` and adds a test that panics on `master`.

### Context

We’re building new API for creating/update routes (/QTS) that’s decoupled from TRN allocation and more-closely aligns with the TRS data model.
So that Register and AfQTS can migrate independently of the route migration to TRS, these new API endpoints should first be built over DQT.
This ticket out the implementation on top of DQT so that Register and AfQTS can migrate away from the old v2 API.

author: pitsteinbach
body:
With this PR I want to introduce DMP solvers implemented in our `GAMBITS` library to `tblite`. Additionally, a `cuSOLVER´-based  DSYGVD solver is also added. `GAMBITS` depends on LAHVA which provides a BLAS LAPACK interface with easy switching between CPU and GPU based execution.
In general we would need to discuss how our CD/CI can test for GPU builds.

There are also a few changes in this PR that affect the solver type, those are mainly needed when interfacing `tblite` to CREST or another program based on MD simulations where we would like to have a solver that can exist for multiple singlepoint calculations. Additional work, will also be needed in `CREST` but that is also prepared.

Further details about the method and it's implementation can be found here: https://chemrxiv.org/engage/chemrxiv/article-details/678e35ecfa469535b9c804c4

ToDos:

- [x] CI/CD adaptation for GPU builds
- [x] documentation on how to build for GPUs
- [x] documentation on DMP shemes

author: austinmatherne-wk
body:
#### Reason for change
For the JSON log the same object is used for storing the message text (`text` key) along with the message arguments. If there is [an arg with the key name](https://github.com/Arelle/EDGAR/blob/4196818170991c916f6a40c73c0e115484f23f03/render/resources/arelleMessagesText.xml#L1681) `text` it overwrites the message text.

This update moves the arguments to a separate object in the json log so names don't collide.

#### Description of change
Move log message args to "args" object in JSON log.

#### Steps to Test
* CI

@Arelle/arelle

- [ ] Output Documentation in `docs/output.md` is updated.
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` is updated.
- [ ] `README.md` is updated (including new tool citations and authors/contributors).

author: clackyai[bot]
body:
- Implemented blog cover image functionality

#### Key Changes
- Added cover image support to the Post model using Active Storage.
- Updated the admin posts controller to handle cover image uploads.
- Modified the article form to include a cover image upload field.
- Modified the view templates to display the cover image on the article detail page and the article list page.
- Added a default cover image and helper method.
- Fixed redundant display of cover images on blog content pages.
- Added cover image display functionality on the homepage and blog listing pages.
- Installed and configured the libvips image processing library to optimize image processing performance.

#### Rationale
This change introduces the ability to add cover images to blog posts, enhancing the visual appeal and user experience.

#### Impact
This change impacts the Post model, admin posts controller, view templates, stylesheets, and database schema. It also requires the installation of the libvips image processing library.

Snyk has created this PR to upgrade bcryptjs from 2.4.3 to 3.0.2.

:information_source: Keep your dependencies up-to-date. This makes it easier to fix existing vulnerabilities and to more quickly identify and fix newly disclosed vulnerabilities when they affect your project.
⚠️ **Warning:** This PR contains major version upgrade(s), and may be a breaking change. - The recommended version is **3 versions** ahead of your current version. - The recommended version was released **a month ago**.
Release notes
Package name: bcryptjs
  • 3.0.2 - 2025-02-18

    Bug fixes

    • Use upstream fix to emit interop helpers (28e5103)
  • 3.0.1 - 2025-02-17

    Bug fixes

    • Separate ESM and UMD type definitions (e7055ca)
  • 3.0.0 - 2025-02-13

    Breaking changes

    • Modernize project structure (2f45985)
      The project now exports an ECMAScript module by default, albeit with an UMD fallback, ships with types, the dist/ directory no longer exists in version control, and Closure Compiler externs have been removed.
    • Generate 2b hashes by default (d36bfb4)
      This library was not affected by the bug that led to incrementing the bcrypt version from 2a to 2b, but nowadays most implementations use 2b, including the native bcrypt binding, so this change aligns with them. Existing hashes will continue to work, but test logic that generates hashes and compares them literally might need to be updated to account for the new default.

    Features

    • Add helper to check for password input length (d5656b3)

    Other

    • Update publish workflow (2a9bea9)
    • Add note on using the ESM variant in the browser (e09eb9a)
    • Update types (58333a1)

author: glormph
body:
This PR will prepare the backend for the coming multi-storage-file possibility, but will not change anything for the user.

- A storedfile will have related model with servershare/path/purged (deleted stays on storedfile), which it can have multiple of, as not to have to duplicate rows there (before this PR a storedfile has servershare/path, and is also not expected to be duplicated except for mzMLs etc). Yes, that means a lot of refactoring, we need to know what to pass to different jobs, what to return to the user UI, etc etc. A problem arising from this is that job args will change, invalidating older jobs - so we'll have to do some cleaning up there or migrate existing jobs.
- Servershare gets max data security level, so we can decide whether we are allowed to store personal data there or not. This does not currently do anything yet.
- No more moving to primary servershare

Transfer jobs to move files between servers and the logic for what goes where will be implemented later.

__Prepare before deploying:__
- [x] Clean up or migrate existing jobs so they wont all crash
- [x] Home view by hand (no test coverage)
- [x] Do not forget to commit the migrations

__Test the following by hand on new system, due to there not being full coverage:__
- [x] Convert mzML
- [x] Backups/retrieval
- [x] Run analysis
- [ ] Old mzML deletion

body:
## `model/account.go` has a potential SQL injection vulnerability on line 61 @chrisyoonullify has asked me to open this fix PR You can see more details about this risk on the Nullify dashboard [here](https://app.chrisyoonullify.dev.nullify.ai/dashboard/findings/code/?id=01JQ668S2F017VENFN8HA1H8GE).
The vulnerability exists because user input (`a.Name`) is directly interpolated into the SQL query string using `fmt.Sprintf()`. This allows an attacker to inject malicious SQL code that could manipulate the query's logic, potentially leading to unauthorized data access or manipulation.
```diff diff --git a/model/account.go b/model/account.go index 6241331..6abdab2 100644 --- a/model/account.go +++ b/model/account.go @@ -61,5 +61,5 @@ func (a *Account) FindByName(rep repository.Repository, name string) (*Account, func (a *Account) Create(rep repository.Repository) (*Account, error) { - query := fmt.Sprintf(`SELECT name, password, authority_id FROM account_master WHERE name = %s`, a.Name) + query := `SELECT name, password, authority_id FROM account_master WHERE name = ?` - result := rep.Exec(query) + result := rep.Exec(query, a.Name) if result.Error != nil { ```
The fix replaces string interpolation with parameterized queries by: 1. Changing the query to use a placeholder (`?`) instead of directly embedding the variable 2. Passing the variable (`a.Name`) as a separate parameter to the `Exec()` function ```diff - query := fmt.Sprintf(`SELECT name, password, authority_id FROM account_master WHERE name = %s`, a.Name) + query := `SELECT name, password, authority_id FROM account_master WHERE name = ?` - result := rep.Exec(query) + result := rep.Exec(query, a.Name) ``` This ensures that the input is properly escaped and treated as data rather than executable code.
## To prevent this again To prevent SQL injection vulnerabilities in the future: 1. Always use parameterized queries or prepared statements instead of string concatenation or interpolation for SQL queries 2. Implement input validation to reject potentially malicious inputs 3. Follow the principle of least privilege for database accounts used by the application 4. Consider using an ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) library that handles SQL injection protection automatically 5. Conduct regular security code reviews focusing on data access patterns 6. Include SQL injection testing in your security testing procedures

author: jesskelsall
body:
# What's changed

Redesigns the search experience based around search always being part of the nav-bar rather than an element of each page. As a result this is a sweeping change that impacts multiple places on the website.

These changes are **not** behind the `concepts-v1` feature flag - this is because the header/nav-bar is present on every page and introducing an asynchronous feature flag check on each page would be horrendous. I'm happy to be challenged on this.

- Add new components:
  - `NavSearchDropdown`: a straightforward two-option dropdown for choosing the search input's context. Originally I built this with Base UI's `select` component but a bespoke component was needed to get everything right.
  - `NavSearch`: the search bar now present in the nav-bar. Uses our `Input` component + `NavSearchDropdown`.
    - Shows a search context dropdown on certain pages with specific context wording.
    - Context and current page determines what happens when searching.
    - Quite a bit of fussing around UX, particularly when using a keyboard.
    - Pop-around search results box including geographies (improved sorting, bold on matched substring) and a generic search option.
    - Sticky (remains at the top of the page on scroll). Minor reworks needed to the overall page layout to acommodate.
  - `NavBar`
    - Replaces `PageHeader`.
    - Logo, menu, and additional styling is now passed as props, so this component is now used for all 3 sites.
- Storybook:
  - Support for routing and `QueryClient` which now wraps all components (Storybook decorator).
  - `NavSearch`
  - `NavBar` with examples from CPR, CCLW, and MCF.
- `NavBar` implementation:
  - CPR: Replaces what was previously in `layouts/main.tsx`.
  - CCLW/MCF: Replaces what was previously in `components/Header.tsx`.
    - Accounts for route-specific styling, as these sites use `NavBar` on their homepages.
- Removed search from existing places:
  - This involved tidying up UI where other elements appeared next to the search input.
  - `FloatingSearch` from old nav-bar (deleted component).
  - `DocumentSearchForm` from document page (deleted component).
  - `SearchForm` from everywhere else (one last usage in `ConceptsDocumentViewer.tsx`).

Potential later tweaks:
- `NavSearch` position and width at different breakpoints, particularly for CCLW due to how its logo is two compound images.

body:
## Route Structure

| Path | Component | Authentication | Description |
|------|-----------|----------------|-------------|
| `/login` | `Login` | Public | Login page |
| `/signup` | `Signup` | Public | Sign up page |
| `/todo-lists` | `TodoLists` | Protected | Main application view for managing todo lists |
| `/` | `Navigate` | Redirect | Redirects to `/todo-lists` |

## Authentication Flow

- **Public routes** (`/login`, `/signup`) are accessible to all users
- **Protected routes** are wrapped with the `ProtectedRoute` component which:
  - Checks if a user is authenticated
  - Redirects unauthenticated users to the login page
  - Allows authenticated users to access the requested route
- Redirects authenticated users to `/todo-lists` if visiting `/login` or `/signup`

body:
When using the Sale Partner Address Restrict module, you are forced to use invoice and delivery addresses related to the main customer.

When selling to a dropshipper, the delivery address represents a final end customer that is not part of the main customer, but it is still useful to have the relation in the system so that you know which dropship addresses have been created for each of your dropshipper customers.

With the new checkbox you can mark dropship delivery addresses to ensure that the dropshipper name is not displayed for them. This will hide it from the PDF reports.

# Codebase Cleanup and Standardization

## Overview
This PR represents a comprehensive cleanup of the codebase focusing on consistency, maintainability, and user experience improvements. No new features were added - instead, the focus was on standardizing patterns, removing redundancy, and improving error handling and loading states.

## Changes

### 🏗️ Code Structure
- Created central `types/` directory with shared type definitions
- Consolidated duplicate utilities and merged filters
- Replaced legacy RBAC methods with unified permission system
- Organized auth-related code with consistent patterns

### 🧩 Component Improvements
- Created reusable `AuthForm` and `FormField` components
- Enhanced `SubmitButton` with better loading state handling
- Removed deprecated `header-auth.tsx` component
- Simplified admin routes with shared redirect component

### ⚡ Performance & UX
- Added loading indicators throughout the application using Next.js 15 loading.tsx convention
- Implemented skeleton UI for structured content areas
- Improved error handling with graceful degradation
- Enhanced client-side loading states for better feedback

### 📝 Documentation
- Added `CHANGELOG.md` to track version history
- Updated `README.md` with project details and structure
- Created comprehensive `TODO.md` with completed work summary
- Added better code comments where needed

### 🐛 Bug Fixes
- Fixed permission checking function to properly check against PERMISSIONS map
- Standardized snake_case vs. camelCase inconsistencies in types
- Improved error handling in components and utilities

## Testing Notes
The changes maintain all existing functionality while improving code quality. Testing should focus on:
- Authentication flows (login, signup, password reset)
- Admin and user dashboard functionality
- Loading states during navigation and data operations
- Error handling with graceful degradation

author: elfedy
body:
# What :computer: 
Adds `verify-bytecode` support. Since ZKsync does not have deployment code, only the runtime bytecode is compared directly with the onchain bytecode without local instantiation of the vm to get the `deployedBytecode`, and without checking constructor arguments. There could be a case for running this instantiation to check invariant values but since the bytecode is immutable, same constructor arguments should yield same invariants and the added overhead to run this check did not seem worth it.

Even though we do not retrieve constructor arguments, we still need a block explorer with the verified contract in order to determine the `hash_type` the contract was compiled with as there is no trivial way to find out what metadata hash was used from the bytecode alone, and each type requires different handling to get the raw bytecode. We also get the settings to compare them to the local settings in case of a mismatch.

TODO: Get an etherscan key we can use either in secrets or leave as public (as upstream does) to add etherscan test. 

# Why :hand:
Closes https://github.com/matter-labs/foundry-zksync/issues/615

# Evidence :camera:
Added tests pass. Commented etherscan test passes when adding a valid etherscan key.

author: lars18th
body:
This PR adds the functionality to compile the binary blob of each firmware that is used (not all existing ones) with the modules that use it. This increases the module size, but only a bit. As a benefit no firmware files or kernel support is needed to load the module. Also, this change does not remove the option to load non-embedded firmwares. The functionality is still there. It's only necessary to delete the firmware file before compiling, and provide the normal file inside /lib/modules afterwards.

The use cases for this:
- When the kernel has dynamic firmware loading disabled.
- When you want to use the kernel modules independently.
- When you don't want to distribute additional firmwares.

The patch works using three different scripts:
- firmware_fw.pl: Prepares the blob from .fw files by generating .h files.
- firmware_header.pl: Patches the .h files that load the firmwares if the blob exists.
- firmware_source.pl: Patches the .c files to use the new functions request/release_firmware().

Fully tested and reliable.

author: ivolnistov
body:
**Technical explanation of the issue:**

1. When using 'fork', a copy of the current process is created, including memory and state of all objects. This means logging settings are preserved.
2. When using 'spawn', a new process is created which imports modules fresh. This means all global objects, including loggers, are initialized again.

**Problem in taskiq code:**

1. Logging configuration happens in the parent process, but these settings are not passed to child processes when using 'spawn'.
2. DEBUG logs are not visible because by default loggers in child processes have WARNING or INFO level.

**PR fixes:**

1. This PR fixes the logging issue when using the 'spawn' method in multiprocessing
2. Adds log-format support, which allows more flexible configuration of logger behavior when using spawn

Now DEBUG level logs will be correctly displayed in all child processes, even when using the 'spawn' method, and log formatting settings can be easily customized.

This PR includes several improvements and bug fixes, along with some work-in-progress updates for upcoming features:

#### Features
- **New `/models` Endpoint & CORS Support:**  
  Introduces a new `/models` endpoint and enables CORS to facilitate cross-origin requests.

#### Bug Fixes
- **Multi Tool Accumulation & Buffer Leak:**  
  Fixes the bug causing multi tool accumulation and resolves the mid-response tool buffer leak.
- **Chat Completions Data Models:**  
  Updates the `FunctionDetail` model and removes the `name` field from `ToolCall` to ensure the chat completions pydantic models meet current requirements.

#### Chores
- **Tool Patterns Update:**  
  Refines tool patterns to improve consistency and maintainability.

#### Work in Progress (WIP)
- **MCP Client & Tool Registry:**  
  The MCP client and tool registry are now functional, marking progress toward full integration.
- **Agent Configuration:**  
  The MCP configuration in `agent.yaml` is commented out by default to prevent accidental activation until it’s fully stable.

body:
# Implement Function to Find Common Array Element with O(n) Time Complexity

## Original Task
Write a function that takes two arrays as inputs and returns true if they have at least one common element, otherwise return false. The function should have a time complexity of O(n).

## Summary of Changes
Added a new function to efficiently detect if two arrays have at least one common element using a hash set approach.

## Acceptance Criteria
All tests must pass. The function must take two arrays as input. Must return true if the arrays share at least one common element. Must return false if no common elements exist. Must achieve O(n) time complexity.

## Tests
 - Test function with arrays containing a common element
 - Test function with arrays having no common elements
 - Test function with empty arrays
 - Test function with large arrays to verify O(n) performance

author: lalver1
body:
Closes #2721 

This PR  implements the `ClaimsVerificationRequest` refactor. We first add a `claims_request` field (which is a foreign key to `ClaimsVerificationRequest`, a new model from `cdt_identity`) to `EnrollmentFlow`, migrate data from `EnrollmentFlow` to `ClaimsVerificationRequest`, and finally remove from `EnrollmentFlow`

-  `claims_scope`
- `claims_eligibility_claim`
- `claims_extra_claims`
- `claims_scheme_override`

since they now reside in `ClaimsVerificationRequest`. This schematic shows how the fields for `EnrollmentFlow` ended up:

| `EnrollmentFlow`                      | `ClaimsVerificationRequest`    |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------- |
|         `id`                                    |               `id`                         |
| `system_name`                        |         `system_name`           |
| ~`claims_scope`~                       |                      `scopes`         |  
| ~`claims_eligibility_claim`~         |  `eligibility_claim`                 |  
| ~`claims_extra_claims`~             |  `extra_claims`                     |  
| ~`claims_scheme_override`~     |          `scheme`                    |  
| `claims_request` (`ClaimsVerificationRequest fk`)                  |
| `...`                                           |                               |

## To review

- Checkout `main`
- Set `DJANGO_DB_FIXTURES` to `local_fixtures.json` and run `bin/reset_db.sh` to reset your database
- Switch to this PR's branch
- Run `bin/init.sh` to run the migrations in this branch and test that the data was migrated successfully from `EnrollmentFlow` to `ClaimsVerificationRequest` and that `claims_request` in `EnrollmentFlow` points to the correct `ClaimsVerificationRequest`
- Start a debugger 
- Log in to the admin with your Google SSO account and enter valid values for any flow that uses the IdG (you can use `Older Adult`):
  - Identity gateway configs -> Client id
  - Identity gateway configs -> Authority
  - Claims verification requests -> Scopes
  - Claims verification requests -> Eligibility claim
- Test the user facing flow that you configured and also test the admin using `calitp-user`
- Test the local developer environment, ensure that the fixtures have been updated and that they successfully load by running `bin/reset_db.sh`
