body: Related to # https://github.com/Automattic/loop/issues/596 ## Proposed Changes Resolves an issue with the facebook sharing popup being too small and looking bad for logged out facebook users. * Updates the facebook popups window width to 1000px to accomodate the facebook login screen that is redirected to if the user is not logged in. unfortunately this login screen by facebook is not device responsive. * This makes the current sharing window larger for logged in facebook users, but it still feels good on my end. * Updates both X and Facebook sharing links to open in a new tab instead of a new window, if the new window would be wider than their current browser window. The alternative to this could be to leave things the way they are. If a user is sharing to another platform, chances are they are logged into that platform. If the increased width for logged in facebook sharing feels too large, leaving it the way it was could be a tradeoff as most users should not experience the issue and those that do shouldn't experience it anymore after they are logged into their platform. Thoughts? BEFORE AFTER ## Why are these changes being made? * A poor popup experience for logged out facebook users, due to facebooks lack of responsive web design 🙃 ## Testing Instructions * Run this branch, logged out of facebook. * Have your browser >1000px width. * Go to the reader, click "share" and select facebook. * Verify the login screen from facebook is more visible and feels less broken. * Decrease the browser screen width to less than 1000px and try again. * Verify the login screen opens in a new tab. * Test with logged-in facebook as well, verify it works as expected. * Test sharing with X - note instead of 1000px for X, the cutoff for window vs. tab for X sharing is 550px width. * Verify this works as expected. * Consider - is this better? Hi!

Thank you for making an admin request on this repo. We strive to make a decision
on these requests within 24 hours.

Cheers and thank you for contributing to conda-forge!
-->

## Guidelines for marking packages as broken:

* We prefer to patch the repo data (see [here](https://github.com/conda-forge/conda-forge-repodata-patches-feedstock))
  instead of marking packages as broken. This alternative workflow makes environments more reproducible.
* Packages with requirements/metadata that are too strict but otherwise work are
  not technically broken and should not be marked as such.
* Packages with missing metadata can be marked as broken on a temporary basis
  but should be patched in the repo data and be marked unbroken later.
* In some cases where the number of users of a package is small or it is used by
  the maintainers only, we can allow packages to be marked broken more liberally.
* We (`conda-forge/core`) try to make a decision on these requests within 24 hours.

What will happen when a package is marked broken?

* Our bots will add the `broken` label to the package. The `main` label will remain on the package and this is normal.
* Our bots will rebuild our repodata patches to remove this package from the repodata.
* In a few hours after the `anaconda.org` CDN picks up the new patches, you will no longer be able to install the package from the `main` channel.

author: nachocodoner
body:
<!-- OSS-713 -->

Continues: https://github.com/meteor/meteor/pull/13657

This PR adds a caching strategy for compilation. SWC don’t provide incremental build caching support by default (Babel seems only through meteor-babel), this is usually handled by the bundler. Rspack, and others already use caching to speed up rebuilds. This PR brings a similar approach to Meteor.

Right now, when Meteor rebuilds due to a single file change, it recompiles everything again. SWC makes this fast, but since we recompile all packages and app code sequentially, it adds unnecessary time. With this PR, unchanged files use the cache; changed files get recompiled and the result is cached.

There are two caches: memory and file. I know memory can grow without limit, so I plan to add an LRU cache to keep it bounded, falling back to file cache when needed. Though `meteor-babel` didn't seem [to have a limitation in its cache implementation](https://github.com/meteor/meteor/blob/devel/npm-packages/meteor-babel/cache.js).

See the performance gains compared to the swc-replacement branch this is based on. It's impressive! 🚀

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/074066af-460f-4b2b-91f9-c41ae3b512fe)

> These values reflect performance gains on a small app built with `meteor create --react`. The improvements will become more noticeable in larger, feature-rich applications.

----------------

Side note: These improvements will help when moving to a modern bundler. The modern bundler will handle app code and provide better caching from the external tool. Still, these changes make sure Meteor won't be a bottleneck during development, rebuilding faster and compiling Meteor packages as quickly as possible.

body:
## Summary

### PR: Allow Using a Query Instance in Addition to a Class-String  

This PR adds the ability to use a `Query` instance in addition to a class-string by default.  

#### Before:  
Previously, if I built my schema at runtime like this:  

```php
$config = [
    'types'     => [/*...*/],
    'mutations' => [/*...*/],
    'query'     => [new FindQueryForModel(User::class)]
];

$schema = GraphQL::buildSchemaFromConfig($config);
```  

I would get the following error:  
`Cannot use object of type FindQueryForModel as array`  

#### Changes:  
- I have added tests.  
- I have handled instantiated `Field` objects by adding a specific case in `GraphQL.php -> buildObjectTypeFromFields`:  

```php
elseif ($field instanceof Field) {
    $field = $field->toArray();
}
```  

#### Documentation:  
I have **not** documented this possibility in `README.md` because it would be a bad practice to use this in the config file. Doing so would break Laravel's caching mechanism, as this type is not serializable.

## Issue tracking
Closes #3216, #3215

## Context behind the change
<!--
  What changes have you made to the code, and why?

  Describe the goal of this pull request. What does it change or fix?
  At a high level, what parts of the code did you change and why?
-->

## How has this been tested?
- [x] locally e2e; sign in as operator; make it active, then deactivate

## Release plan
As part of parent PR w/o extra steps

## Potential risks; What to monitor; Rollback plan
After FE runs enable/disable operation, it does refresh of auth tokens because  jwt stores `operator_status`. When adding `operator_status` to JWT, we first read its value from KV store, so there is a risk of reading a stale value from subgraph in many cases. Same applies to scenario when you e.g. deactivate operator and immediately attempt to activate it: RepO has a validation on operator status before calling `KV.set`, so operation may fail.

In order to alleviate this replication lag, after activating/deactivating operator we manually update its data in browser memory in order to display valid status. However if refreshed token has stale value and user refreshes the browser page - they will still see outdated value. In case we find an issue in it - let's address it in separately.

author: whsieh
body:
#### 1f4f2000ed16188b1eecbfdd36bf58e623142390 
[iOS] [SelectionHonorsOverflowScrolling] Caret sometimes appears in the wrong place after inserting newline
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=290393
rdar://147362685

Reviewed by Aditya Keerthi.

With SelectionHonorsOverflowScrolling enabled, inserting (or deleting) newlines inside a `textarea`
sometimes causes the caret to appear in the wrong place, if the editing command triggered
programmatic scrolling in the `textarea`'s content. This is due to 2 main causes:

1.  `-_reconcileEnclosingScrollViewContentOffset:` yields incorrect `EditorState` geometry in the
    case where scrolling is triggered by the web process itself (and the scroll position is being
    synced to the UI process through the same layer tree commit that contains this `EditorState`).
    From manually testing the scenario in 286537@main (i.e. composing an email in Outlook and Gmail)
    this logic is only needed in the case where the user begins scrolling a scroll view that
    contains the selection UI, such that the child scroller is in unstable state (and therefore, the
    UI-side `-contentOffset` holds the source of truth, regarding the scroll offset of the scroller
    containing the selection). To mitigate this, limit the codepath to trigger only when the scroll
    view is in unstable state.

2.  Add a mechanism to call into `-[UITextSelectionDisplayInteraction setNeedsSelectionUpdate]`
    (via `WKTextInteractionWrapper`) in the case where a subscroller containing the selection has
    been scrolled and the geometry of the `EditorState` in root view coordinates is still the same
    as it was during the previous update. Even ignoring (1), when inserting or removing a newline at
    the end of a `textarea`, it's possible for the caret rect to *immediately* become stale, if the
    caret view is installed before the `-contentOffset` of the subscroller changes after inserting
    or deleting at the end of the `textarea`. In this case, a subsequent `EditorState` update will
    not update the selection at all since the caret rect in root view coordinates is identical, even
    if the caret rect in the coordinate space of the view containing the selection changes.

    We can mitigate this by calling into `-setNeedsSelectionUpdate` in this case, which tells UIKit
    to remap root view coordinates into selection container coordinates and reposition managed
    selection views accordingly. Note that without this part, inserting and removing newlines
    *sometimes* still causes the caret to be positioned incorrectly (either one line too high or one
    line too low) when typing near the last line of a vertically scrollable `textarea`.

See below for more details.

* LayoutTests/editing/selection/ios/caret-rect-after-inserting-newlines-in-textarea-expected.txt: Added.
* LayoutTests/editing/selection/ios/caret-rect-after-inserting-newlines-in-textarea.html: Added.
* Source/WebKit/UIProcess/API/ios/WKWebViewIOS.h:
* Source/WebKit/UIProcess/API/ios/WKWebViewIOS.mm:
(-[WKWebView _isInStableState:]):

Expose a method to check whether a given `UIScrollView` is in stable state, using heuristics which
currently only apply to the main scroller (`WKScrollView`).

* Source/WebKit/UIProcess/ios/WKContentViewInteraction.h:
* Source/WebKit/UIProcess/ios/WKContentViewInteraction.mm:
(-[WKContentView cleanUpInteraction]):
(-[WKContentView _scrollingNodeScrollingDidEnd:]):

Keep track of whether we've just ended scrolling inside a scroll view that contains the current
selection, but haven't received an editor state update yet that honors this new scroll position.
This flag (`_waitingForEditorStateAfterScrollingSelectionContainer`) allows us to bail from updating
the selection with stale geometry in `-_updateSelectionViewsInChildScrollViewIfNeeded`, in the case
where momentum scrolling ends in a subscrollable region containing the selection (undoing this
results in a 1-frame flicker of the selection when scrolling the compose window on Gmail).

(-[WKContentView _reconcileEnclosingScrollViewContentOffset:]):

See (1) above.

(-[WKContentView _updateChangedSelection:]):
(-[WKContentView _updateSelectionViewsInChildScrollViewIfNeeded]):

See (2) above.

# Test Plan for DSE Behavior in Version 1.78  

## 1. New Users on Version 1.78  
- Default Search Engine (DSE) is set to **Yahoo! JAPAN**.  

## 2. Upgrade from Version 1.77 to 1.78  
- **If the user did not modify the DSE in version 1.77:**  
  - If DSE was **Yahoo! JAPAN** → It remains **Yahoo! JAPAN** in 1.78.  
  - If DSE was **Google** → It changes to **Yahoo! JAPAN** in 1.78.  
  - If DSE was **any other search engine (excluding Google/Yahoo! JAPAN)** → It remains unchanged in 1.78.  

- **If the user modified the DSE in version 1.77:**  
  - The user's chosen DSE is respected in 1.78.  

## 3. Direct Upgrade from Version ≤ 1.76 to 1.78  
- If DSE was **Google** → It changes to **Yahoo! JAPAN** in 1.78.  
- If DSE was **any search engine other than Google** → It remains unchanged in 1.78.  

## 4. Upgrade Path: Version ≤ 1.76 → 1.77 → 1.78  
- If DSE was **Google** in 1.76:  
  - If the user **did not modify** DSE in 1.77 → It changes to **Yahoo! JAPAN** in 1.78.  
  - If the user **changed DSE to another search engine (e.g., DDG) in 1.77** → It remains as that search engine in 1.78.  
  - If the user **changed DSE to another search engine (e.g., DDG) and then back to Google in 1.77** → It remains **Google** in 1.78.  

- If DSE was **any search engine other than Google (e.g., DDG) in 1.76**:  
  - If the user **did not modify** DSE in 1.77 → It remains unchanged in 1.78.

body:
#### What this PR does

Adds a new metric to track problems with HA. According to [this note](https://grafana.com/docs/mimir/latest/configure/configure-high-availability-deduplication/#distributor-high-availability-ha-tracker), if the first series in the request happens to be incorrectly configured, HA will not work properly for all the other series in the request. If I'm understanding how this works correctly, this means that for users with a lot of series, if only a minority of them are configured incorrectly, it can be very hard to track down the problem. This PR tries to fix that by using a new metric to show the metric names of the series that are misconfigured, and the reason why the HA fails e.g. is it the cluster or replica label that's missing? It also adds a log line with more details.

This could potentially create a lot of new series and log lines, so it's behind a per-tenant config flag `track_ha_failures` (off by default) so we can turn it on only temporarily for users as needed.

Will update changelog after getting feedback on this approach.

author: rubennorte
body:
Summary:
Changelog: [internal]

## Context

We have some tests that make sure certain objects are deallocated/released at the right times, but those are generally hard to get right. The main reason is that WeakRefs semantics are tied to the tasks and microtasks in JS, but we handle them both inside and outside the Event Loop in Fantom tests.

This leads to some surprising behavior where things we expect to have been deallocated weren't because of some innocent looking code.

## Changes

This introduces a safety mechanism in Fantom to enforce that WeakRefs are always dereferenced inside the Event Loop, by patching the method in `WeakRef` and checking if we're in the Event Loop using Fantom APIs.

It also updates the existing test using WeakRefs to fix the new errors thrown by this patch, and to serve as a "good example" on how to use WeakRefs to do memory testing.

Reviewed By: yungsters

author: metagn
body:
`succ` and `pred` are added that are valid versions of `+`/`-` for a generic `Ordinal` type. `inc` and `dec` now use these and are defined for `Ordinal`. This means we can define `..` and `..<` on `Ordinal` as well and use `Ordinal` instead of a concept for the index type in `default` for arrays.

Versions of `<`, `<=`, `==` are also added for `Ordinal`. This caused issues with the overload for `enum` since `Ordinal` and `enum` did not match each other and so generic disambiguation did not work, now `enum` matches `Ordinal` but not vice versa so it works. We can also just remove the overload for `enum` so generic disambiguation does not trigger at all.

The `==` operator for strings used in `case` for strings now aliases a `equalStrings` proc so we don't have problems with the `==` order in system anymore.

A downside of `..`/`..<` being generic is that modules will keep creating their own instantiations but iterators get eliminated anyway. We could add concrete overloads for `int` etc, but a problem with specializations like this is that the generic overload will match in typed generics and so the specialized overload will not be used for the instantiation. Though this isn't as much of a problem for `..` since the operands aren't usually generic, but the gain isn't too much either.

<!-- Write **BELOW** The Headers and **ABOVE** The comments else it may not be viewable. -->
<!-- You can view Contributing.MD for a detailed description of the pull request process. -->

## About The Pull Request

This PR makes all melee weapons no longer get the justice buff when dealing damage to humans in City Gamemodes
Also, This buffs all of the blade lineage weapons by making their empowered attack deal 2% more damage per 1% HP they have.

## Why It's Good For The Game

For the gamemodes where PVP is most likely to happen, it ends rather quickly. And with how damage on weapons accounts for dealing with mobs which have over 750 HP on average (At high levels when PVP happens), while humans are only able to have a max of 260 HP, causes the weapons to be overturned for PVP. This nerf should make PVP more interesting, since players will have time to think about their actions, instead of everything ending under 3 seconds.

Also, With these buffs it would make BL very weak since they relay on ending fights in one hit, So this buff should help them deal more damage. Along with the justice nerf, it will let them take more hits before going down.

## Summary

This pull request introduces optimizations to reduce gas consumption, enhance security, and improve code efficiency. The changes primarily involve replacing external calls with internal function calls, optimizing existing functions, and making the codebase more concise.

## Changes made
- Created an internal _getNFTCategory function

  - Replaced the external getNFTCategory function with an internal _getNFTCategory.
  - Eliminated the need for self-calls, reducing gas consumption.
  - Improved efficiency by allowing direct access to internal state.

 - Optimized the _exists function
   - Replaced the try/catch block with a direct state check: _ownerOf(tokenId) != address(0).
   - Avoids unnecessary execution overhead and reduces the risk of re-entrancy issues.
   - More efficient and safer implementation.

- Updated function calls to use internal _getNFTCategory
- Replaced all instances of this.getNFTCategory() with _getNFTCategory().
- Simplified getUserNFTData function
- Removed unnecessary whitespace and optimized the function structure.
- Enhances code readability and maintainability without altering functionality.

- Deploy the optimized contract on the testnet for further validation.
- Gather benchmarking results to quantify gas savings.
- Review any potential edge cases before mainnet deployment.

# Implement Algorithm to Find Closest Points Between Two Lists

## Original Task
Given two lists A and B of points in the Cartesian plane, implement an algorithm that finds the two closest pairs of points in A and B. The distance between two points is the Euclidean distance: sqrt((x1 - x2)^2 + (y1 - y2)^2).

## Summary of Changes
Developed an efficient algorithm to find the two closest pairs of points between two lists of points in the Cartesian plane using Euclidean distance calculation.

## Acceptance Criteria
All tests must pass. The function must calculate Euclidean distance between two points. The input will be two lists of points represented as (x, y) coordinates. The function must return the two closest pairs of points, one from list A and one from list B. The algorithm must handle various input sizes efficiently.

 - Check handling of different input list sizes

body: Closes https://github.com/metabase/metabase/issues/51560 ### Description Improve the performance of the query to check for a user's permission to access a collection by using semi-joins to check if the collection is permitted by any of a user's permissions group memberships. The current query needs to join all the permission data together which means that we check multiple times for any route through group memberships between a user and a collection. Ordinarily this is fine, but leads to polynomial growth based on how many groups a user is a member of. By using a semi-join we can check if a collection is permitted once which reduced query times on my reproduction of the original reporter's setup from 450ms to 22ms. ### How to verify Create a very large number of collections and groups granting permission to view those collections to a given user. Visit the collections page. Should load in under 1s. author: danibalcells
body:
Significant change in the way the dialectic and deriver work.

Before:
- Deriver does the heavy lifting. Generates a new user representation asynchronously for each user message that comes in.
- Dialectic pulls latest user representation as additional context to answer queries.
- Problem: poor management of long-term context. Stores all long-term context as natural language in the user rep, and relies on the inference that updates the user rep to preserve everything useful from the past and add new information.

Now:
- Deriver only extracts facts from incoming messages and stores them in an embedding document store.
- Dialectic generates a user representation on the fly that's tailored to the query.
- Two steps in parallel:
  - Short-term: get current chat history and run TOM inference on it.
  - Long-term: based on dialectic query, generate 3-5 queries for the document store. Retrieve 30-50 facts.
- User representation is the concatenation of the TOM inference and the long-term facts

author: haoranyi
body:
#### Problem

StorableAccountsBySlot::Account() fn, which looks up the account by index from a collection of accounts stored across different slots, is widely used in shrink/squash. However, this function use a sequential loop over starting_offsets to find the internal index. Because the start_offset is calculated from cumulative len of accounts in each slot, start_offsets must be never decresing hence it is sorted. Based on this, we can do binary search in stead of sequential looping to find the internal index. 


#### Summary of Changes

Implement a binary search to find internal index for StorableAccountsBySlot.

#### Testing

Running [this branch plus timing stats instrumentation](https://github.com/HaoranYi/solana/tree/bin_search_stat) on mainnet shows that for large number of storage to squash, such as 12K, binary search is 10X faster. 
Note that the number of storages being squashed/shrunk varies a lot. The most common number is 1. But it could be in the range from 1 to 16K. 

Considering squashing16K storages, find_internal_index by looping will need 8K*16K = 128M lookups, while by bin-search only needs 14*16K=224K lookups, much less lookups.

```
bin_search_ns =197,312,537i 
loop_search_ns=1867,956,100i 
arr_size=11745i
```

author: jaylyn-barbee
body:
At the time of this PR only the OCR model works fully on Intel Copilot+ PCs. 

You are able to download both the ImageScaler and ImageSegmentation models, via `.isAvailable` or `.MakeAvailable` however, they fail at the `.CreateAsync` step. 

Both Phi Silica and Image describer fail at the `.isAvailable` step which makes them "undetectable" when on an Intel Copilot+ PC.

This enables the Intel NPU to be found and adds error handling to handle the above errors. Unfortunately, for the two models that fail at `.isAvailable` we are unable to tell whether that means we are not on a C+PC or if we are and they just aren't supported yet, so it shows the "You need a C+PC to use this sample" (paraphrasing) message. The only work around to fix this message would be assuming having an NPU implies C+PC but this is not necessarily always true.

body:
- Adding a test for remote upgrade with a large Wasm file ( as much as a transaction can handle which is around 1.5 MB ). It shows that the problem that was earlier described with the exceeded prepaid gas error, does not occur within that size limit. It might have been a problem with the previous transaction limit of 4 MB, see my comment here: https://github.com/near-daos/sputnik-dao-contract/issues/222#issuecomment-2752000490.
- Fixed compiler warnings in the test code.
- Even though it makes no difference for the test to pass, I've changed `upgrade_remote` to use `promise_batch_action_function_call_weight` for passing on the remaining gas.
- In addition, changed to use `promise_batch_action_function_call_weight` all places where subtracting used gas from prepaid gas. ( this was also not broken, so a bit against the principle of "if it ain't broken, don't fix it" )
- New updated Wasm binaries. Note that even with reproducible builds, all of the contract Wasms has differences. Some contracts are not changed in this PR, and so not all should be changed like you can see here. We should also discuss the need for having the Wasm files in the repo, since the tests always needs to build them anyway. When working locally on Silicon Macs, reproducible builds are challenging, since the docker builds requests the `linux/amd64` platform, and you'd rather want to build non-reproducible when working locally.

body:
(For review only, we won't actually merge this.)

leanprover/lean4#7672 makes many changes to the implicitness of arguments in the List/Array/Vector APIs. Mostly the consequences in Mathlib are positive: we get to remove many `_`s!

However at times we now need named arguments.

In cases where we are writing "uphill" by a lemma, I don't so much mind the extra notation of named arguments.

However if reviewers see things here where they would prefer to just have an explicit argument, please let me know. Even if leanprover/lean4#7672 is already in I'm happy to revert some of the changes.

body:
Reduced from 66 to 37 classes in minimal codegen config.

## Changes

Removed classes:
- left over from examples
- which didn't have a real purpose, and an existing class could take their place
- which are now only run in `codegen-full` itest mode

## Compile times

Build time of `godot-core` crate with `cargo build --timings`, after `cargo clean`:

| `cargo` command | Branch | Times |
|----|----|----|
|`build -p itest --no-default-features`| this PR | 4.58s, 5.1s, 5.49s
|`build -p itest --no-default-features`| `master` | 5.47, 5.65s, 6.32s
|`build -p itest`| `master` | 20.75s, 20.98s, 21.31s


Result of `hyperfine` -- on this PR and master:
```rs
Benchmark 1: cargo clean && cargo build -p godot-core --no-default-features
  Time (mean ± σ):      8.144 s ±  0.418 s    [User: 14.440 s, System: 2.439 s]
```

```rs
Benchmark 1: cargo clean && cargo build -p godot-core --no-default-features
```

author: superronan
body:
As mentioned in #6601, generic interface specialization were missing an export tag -> they are considered as dead code -> can't link them in later compilation stages. 
The solution was to check when specializing an interface if it had an export tag, and create a new export tag for the specialization.
I wrote a basic IR mangler to generate the specialized export tag, but it is probably not a very durable solution (Is there already an IR mangler? I did not find one). 

Closes #6601.

author: dgelessus
body:
Fixes #1677.

The field `plMouseEventMsg::fWheelDelta` was uninitialized by default and thus had an unpredictable value (which may or may not be 0) for most mouse events. This made the code for fading out the cursor sometimes wrongly think that the player is constantly scrolling, which prevented the cursor from ever fading out.

The underlying bug (the uninitialized field) has always been there since the original open-source release, but went unnoticed, because apparently nothing used the field. It only became noticeable recently with #1653, which added code to reset the cursor fade out timer upon scrolling.

author: tomweston
body:
Adds a new exercise `exercise-04-resource-protection.md` to the `module-03-stacks-and-programs` section of the foundational training. The exercise teaches users how to implement Pulumi's resource protection feature to prevent accidental deletion of critical infrastructure resources.

**The exercise demonstrates:**

- How to conditionally apply resource protection based on stack environment (dev vs prod)
- Creating S3 buckets with protection enabled/disabled based on configuration
- Testing resource protection by attempting to destroy protected resources
- The proper process for removing protection when cleanup is needed
- Best practices for implementing resource protection in production environments

This addition helps users understand an important safety feature for managing production infrastructure and preventing accidental resource deletion that could cause significant disruption.

This PR:

```python
ECCOod._ds['XG'].chunks
>>> ((90,) (2, ), (1, 1))  # respective dims: `mooring`, `Yp1`, `Xp1`
```

This issue is fixed and all test should pass.

body:
## Summary 
This PR merges the feature/routes branch into main, finalizing the core functionality for the general ledger backend. 

## Highlights
 - Ledger Entry Endpoints:

   - Create, read, update, soft delete, and list with filtering support.

    - Includes versioning and idempotency enforcement.

  - Accounts Management:

    - Create, update, and list active accounts.

    - Pre-seeded common account types for use in dropdowns.

  - Summary Endpoint:

    -   /summary returns debit/credit totals, counts, and balanced status with optional filters.

   - Currency Conversion:

     -  Injects live USD → CAD exchange rate (via U.S. Treasury API) into all ledger entry responses as canadian_amount.

## Testing:

   - Unit tests cover all major services: entries, accounts, summaries, and currency.

   - External API calls (exchange rate) are properly mocked for test isolation.

## Dev Enhancements:

 -  Added seed.py and Makefile for faster local development.

 -  Session management cleanup on shutdown.
